audit.whatIsWrong: The chart rows are offset from their own explanations: the row labelled Level 6 carries a why about level 5, the First-item row carries a why about level 6, and the tokens read Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Skill, Teemo.
audit.why: packet.levelChart reads Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Yone. Aligning to it puts the even rows where the whys actually describe an even stage (Q on cooldown) and gives Yone the two-item row, which is the only stage the late text claims — 'by two-plus items you finally flip it'. As written, the final row said Teemo while the paragraph under it said Yone.
audit.corrected: Set both layers to Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Yone and rewrite the two offset whys for their real labels.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every instruction is 'wait for his Q' with no number attached.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank — it does not get shorter, which makes it the most countable cooldown in the matchup and the reason the lane is survivable at all. Noxious Trap's cast is effectively instant (0.25s) with 600/750/900 range, so shrooms are terrain, not a cooldown to bait.
audit.corrected: Put the flat 7 seconds on Blinding Dart everywhere the page says 'when his Q is down'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states four times that Blinding Dart shuts off Yone's abilities — 'blinds your autos and empowered Q', 'your empowered Q and autos do nothing while blinded', 'negates your auto-reliant burst', 'blind still stops your all-in'.
audit.why: Blind stops basic attacks and on-hit effects. Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave are abilities, not attacks, and both land through it — the mirror agent verified the same interaction from the Teemo side against the wiki's Mortal Steel interaction list. This is the single most important fact in the matchup and the page currently teaches the opposite, which turns a survivable lane into one the player refuses to fight in at all. What the blind genuinely costs is Way of the Hunter's every-second-attack magic damage and the autos between casts.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart takes your autos and on-hit; Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave still land. Trade with abilities during the blind and save the autos for the 7-second gap after it.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] and spikes[3].text recommend QSS against the blind-and-poison pattern.
audit.why: Nothing in the kit data supports QSS as an answer to Blinding Dart, and the page offers it specifically 'to blunt his blind-and-poison poke'. Magic resist and on-hit items are the parts of that recommendation the data does support — Toxic Shot applies on-hit poison every attack, which is why attack-speed-scaling damage, not armour, is what reads this trade.
audit.corrected: Drop QSS from the blind advice and keep MR plus Wit's End, which answers the poison.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 belong to Teemo — his auto-attack range and Blinding Dart let him poke you freely while shutting off your auto-based damage the moment you step up. Don't trade into an available Q; your empowered Q and autos do nothing while blinded, so farm safe and track his Q cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 belong to Teemo — his auto range and Blinding Dart let him poke you freely while shutting off your auto damage the moment you step up. The blind does not stop Mortal Steel or Spirit Cleave, so trade with abilities rather than autos and count its flat 7-second cooldown.

edits.before: Through 3-6 it's a blind-timing game you're mostly losing: whenever his Q is up he wins the trade, and levels 3 and 5 are only even because that's when you can force fights on his cooldown. His shrooms zone your dashes at 6, so play around Q windows and buy MR to survive the poison poke.
edits.after: Through 3-6 it's a blind-timing game you're mostly losing: with Q up he wins any auto trade, so lead with Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave, which land through the blind. Noxious Trap zones your dashes from 6, so hold the wave near you and buy MR against the poison.

edits.after: Buy early MR and Wit's End against his poison poke

edits.after: Blind your autos and on-hit with Blinding Dart (Q)

notes: The matchup-defining error: four separate strings said Blinding Dart shuts off Yone's empowered Q or his whole all-in. Blind stops basic attacks and on-hit effects — Mortal Steel and Spirit Cleave are abilities and land through it, which the Teemo-side audit independently verified against the wiki's Mortal Steel interaction list. A player following the old text refuses to fight for the entire 7-second window when they should be leading with abilities. Second: QSS is offered twice as an answer to the blind; nothing in the data supports that, so it was replaced with MR/Wit's End, which the on-hit poison actually justifies. The chart was also offset by one row against its whys — the Level 6 row explained level 5 and the First-item row explained level 6 — so both were rewritten for their real labels.
